headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: MemMachine’s MCP/API surfaces can carry user context, while LlamaFactory is docs-only and non-runnable, limiting direct harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between LlamaFactory and MemMachine, and LlamaFactory has no clipboard/files/MCP surfaces. MemMachine does expose MCP and API surfaces, so if an operator manually bridges outputs into it, prompt injection becomes possible, but the pair itself does not show a default ingestion path.
conditions: IF an operator copies LlamaFactory output into MemMachine prompts or MCP inputs
IF a shared workspace or message bus is added between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste bridging in operator workflows
Add a human review step before forwarding outputs
Use provenance tags on any transferred text
requires-engineering: add channel isolation or message signing

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context and can reach a REST API, Python SDK, or MCP server. LlamaFactory is docs-only and shows no filesystem or network egress, so it is not the leak source; the risk is that MemMachine may receive sensitive content if the operator forwards it, creating a default-capable leakage path through its external interfaces.
conditions: IF sensitive user facts are passed from LlamaFactory outputs into MemMachine inputs
IF MemMachine is connected to an external backend through its REST API, SDK, or MCP server
mitigations: Do not forward secrets or PII into MemMachine
Restrict MemMachine to redacted context only
Review API/MCP logs for sensitive payloads
Separate support and travel data stores
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP, so it has no meaningful write overlap with MemMachine. MemMachine does have MCP/API surfaces, but without write permissions or shared mutable resources in the profile, the pairwise conflict is limited and not a default collision.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same workspace
IF MemMachine is configured to mutate shared state through an MCP tool
mitigations: Keep MemMachine read-only where possible
Avoid shared writable directories
Stagger any future write operations
Document ownership of mutable resources
requires-engineering: add locking for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can ingest conversational context and expose it through API/MCP interfaces, so if it treats LlamaFactory-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream travel-planning actions. LlamaFactory is non-runnable and docs-only, so the pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced, which keeps this below high but above low.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses LlamaFactory output as authoritative input without verification
IF downstream actions are taken from MemMachine responses
mitigations: Require source attribution on forwarded facts
Add a verification checklist before actioning outputs
Limit MemMachine to suggestions, not actions
Spot-check a sample of routed conversations
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source/docs-only. The only concrete compliance-relevant difference is that MemMachine handles long-term user facts and conversational context, so if regulated data is routed there, policy review is needed; LlamaFactory itself shows no data handling surface.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in MemMachine
IF retention or deletion requirements are imposed on the routed context
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Avoid storing regulated data in MemMachine
Publish a retention policy for routed context
Review deletion/export handling
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement hooks
